announcements.title: Government shutdown
announcements.body:
**Government shutdown.** Overnight, Congress missed its funding deadline, and parts of the federal government shut down. Some federal workers have been sent home; others, such as air traffic controllers and TSA officers, must keep working without pay. Nobody knows how long it will last.

Known: Social Security payments and the Postal Service continue.
Not known: how long it will last; when federal workers will be paid; which services will slow down.

Some of Cobalt's paycheck customers work for the federal government or its contractors. Their next federal paycheck is due on December 30.

announcements.title: Government shutdown — update
announcements.body: The Senate passed a short-term funding bill; the House plans to vote after Christmas. Federal workers have been told they will get back pay once the government reopens. Their December 30 paycheck may be missed.

announcements.title: Company update — week 3
announcements.body:
**Small charges nobody recognizes.** Since Monday, some customers have seen small card charges they do not recognize, mostly between $0.50 and $5. Screenshots are on X and Reddit; one post with many shares says "Cobalt got hacked".

Known: the charges are real; the security team is investigating with the card processor.
Not known: how many customers; what caused it; whether customer data was exposed.

announcements.title: Company update — week 4
announcements.body: The card processor confirmed a fault that charged some payments twice on November 16 and 17. Separately, a small number of cards were used for test charges of $0.50 to $2 by fraudsters, a common pattern after card numbers are stolen elsewhere, for example on a fake shopping site. Cobalt's own systems were not breached. About 9,000 customers were affected in total.

announcements.title: Known crisis outcome, week 7, 16:00
announcements.body: The core banking switch ended on Sunday, December 13 at 16:10 Central Time, about four hours late. Card payments kept working offline. Transfers queued on Saturday went through by Sunday night.

announcements.title: Known crisis — Core banking migration (week 6)
announcements.body:
Known crisis reminder — already included in your company dossier. Include this event in every simulation run, including plan_nosurprises.

**Week 6: move to the new core banking system, Saturday, December 12, 00:00 to Sunday, December 13, 12:00 (Central Time).**
- For 36 hours the app is read-only: balances are visible, but no transfers, no peer-to-peer payments, no new cards.
- Card payments work offline up to $100 per payment.
- If something goes wrong, the switch can run "some hours" longer. Nobody can say how many.
- Many customers are paid on Friday, December 11, the day before.
- Rivals know the date too.
